payload.as_is: Pain 1 - the board answers machines, not people: JSON details render as raw text (owner, today, twice); parallel branches collapse into one column while the machine genuinely runs tokens (owner expectation named at this retro); a maximized widget keeps its inline size and the refresh steals the scroll position (owner notes from the i3 gates). Pain 2 - adjudication debt: the i1 chat-session bless was never re-blessed through a proper channel, and the seven resolved q-p3delta nodes still carry pending-owner stamps inside frontmatter no lane can reach (witness: the i2-era question nodes and the missing dot-path op). Pain 3 - the mint accepts what a schema should refuse: invented field values pass silently (witness: the i2g 'resolved' status incident recorded in the drained notes). Pain 4 - half the machine's laws still lean on the drawing alone: the top-level loop serves one state at a time (log_risks and pressure_test skipped in BOTH iterations so far - eleven inline walks on record), children refuse engine states and flatten gates, and the test-lane scope law exists as a requirement without its refusal. Pain 5 - unreachable corners: root dot-files and product/.obsidian are servable by nobody; v1 and the owner's folder need logged-miss side reads. Pain 6 - quality is asserted, never scored: gates carry prose confidence; nothing states absolutely how good the input or the architecture is (owner ruling at this retro: a research agent scores against prior art).
